learning: Iteration 4 (65.14) showed mass 0.5 kg helps the score but leaves one line loss per run on the s-bend and slalom. Iteration 3 showed the sensor offset is not the limit. The body_length result will show whether the remaining yaw inertia is the bottleneck.
notes: Single-variable test of body_length (0.16 to 0.12 m) on the iteration 4 design, with mass 0.5 kg and the iteration 4 controller held exactly. This isolates yaw inertia reduction, which the Builder requested.
rationale: Iteration 4 (mass 0.5 kg, sensor y 0.05 m, body_length 0.16 m, 12 mm footprints, 0.06 m span, wheel_track 0.12 m) is the best design so far at 65.14. Its failure is unchanged: one line loss per run on the s-bend and slalom, with max_error of 0.0666 and 0.0678 m, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit. Iteration 3 showed that moving the sensors forward to y 0.07 m does not remove the loss, and iteration 2 (16 mm footprints, wider span, lighter body) scored lowest, so larger footprints and wider spans have not helped. The Builder's intent is to isolate body_length, which lowers yaw inertia by about 25 percent at fixed mass (0.16 to 0.12 m). I accept this geometry exactly as proposed. The controller is kept identical to iteration 4 (kp 3.0, ki 0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.5, last_direction line loss, weights +1, +0.5, 0, -0.5, -1). Any change in controller would confound the single-variable test the Builder needs. Iteration 1 showed that raising kp and kd did not help, so there is no evidence that more gain is the fix. Expected result, as a prediction only: line losses on the s-bend and slalom fall toward 0.5 or lower and max_error drops below 0.06 m for longer. The race will show whether body_length is the limit.
